name: Beijing E-Town Half-Marathon (Humanoid Robot Half-Marathon)
ability_definition: The ability to exert yourself physically over long periods of time without getting winded or out of breath.

task_realism.reasoning: Sustained bipedal locomotion over 21 km for 2-3 hours directly exercises the core of stamina: continuous physical exertion without breakdown. Real stamina-heavy work is different, though. Warehouse picking, patrol, delivery, construction and caregiving involve multi-hour to full-shift exertion, often with loads, stops and varied movements. A running race is a sport-like proxy, not a workplace task.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The race was on real outdoor roads with a fixed distance and time limit, which adds some ecological validity. However, the rules allowed battery swaps, robot substitutions, remote control and human pacers or helpers. The winning run used three swaps plus teleoperation. That undermines the key condition for stamina, which is sustained exertion without refuelling or external support. The ~3-hour window is also well short of a full work shift, and there were no workplace stakes, payloads or interruptions.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only one slice of stamina: locomotor endurance on fairly uniform terrain. It excludes load carrying, manipulation-heavy exertion and thermal and energy management across a full shift. Swaps and substitutions mean single-charge endurance is not isolated. Finish time also mixes speed with endurance, so the metric only partly captures the 'without getting winded' aspect.

format_match.reasoning: The input is a real physical environment, not a toy or simulated task. The outputs, distance covered and time sustained, map naturally onto endurance requirements such as completing a route or lasting a shift. The race format and completion-time scoring are still artificial compared with work outputs like tasks completed per shift under continuous operation.

transferability_reasoning: The humanoid half-marathon is a real-world, physically grounded test of sustained locomotion, which makes it a more genuine stamina proxy than cognitive or short-duration benchmarks. Its transfer to workplace stamina is limited by several factors. Battery swaps, teleoperation and human assistance were permitted, and the task is locomotion only, with no loads. Speed and endurance are conflated, and the duration is far shorter than a work shift. Together these leave it a moderate-to-weak indicator of whether a robot can sustain real physical work over long periods.

2025.model_or_system: Tiangong Ultra (Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center)
2025.metric: minutes, half-marathon finish time over 21.0975 km (lower is better); 2 h 40 min 42 s = 160.7 min
2025.human_reference: General adult working population, weighted toward workers in physically demanding jobs where stamina matters (construction, warehouse, agriculture). These are not trained runners.
